summary: Replace Tomcat's host error-report valve with one that writes the API's JSON error body (ErrorBodies), so errors the server produces before the application, such as a malformed percent-escape, are JSON on every route; status and headers unchanged.

decisions.choice: Tomcat rejects a malformed request target before the servlet layer and its host's ErrorReportValve renders the page; MVC handlers and the /error controller never see it
decisions.rationale: Confirmed against the packaged jar; the regression tests send raw requests to the real listener

decisions.choice: A TomcatServletWebServerFactory subclass names the valve class on the host before the server starts
decisions.rationale: StandardHost only adds its error-report valve by class name at start; replacing it afterwards would race the start. A named class because the management server is built from the same factory type, so its errors become JSON too (verified)

decisions.choice: Same guards as Tomcat's valve: error status only, nothing written yet, error not yet reported, I/O still allowed; status and headers untouched; body from ErrorBodies.forStatus
decisions.rationale: FR3 and the approved plan: no new error codes and no container details; 405 still carries Allow (verified on the jar)

decisions.choice: 155 tests pass; coverage 91.7% overall, the valve 83.3%; the release smoke steps plus %ZZ on /api and on /, 405 Allow and a management 404 pass on the packaged jar; without the valve the 4 regression tests fail
decisions.rationale: Orchestrator gates re-run all of this
